overview: The Xiongnu were the first great steppe empire, unified under Modu Chanyu and controlling Mongolia and parts of Central Asia. They developed sophisticated cavalry tactics and a dual administrative system that influenced later nomadic empires.

items.text: Composite bows and cavalry tactics made them formidable mounted warriors.
Metalworking for weapons, horse gear and luxury goods.
Ancestor worship and elaborate burial practices for elites.
Controlled trade routes between China and Central Asia.
Extracted tribute and trade goods from agricultural neighbors.
The Xiongnu model of steppe empire influenced later Turkic and Mongol states.
Their name may be the origin of the term Hun in European sources.

fall.text: The Xiongnu confederation fragmented under pressure from the Xianbei and Han Chinese forces.
